notes: Matched units agree most often on actor and policy type. Main disagreements: (1) phase, where coders split between general, course-start, before-course and during-work for the same sentence (resolved by asking when the rule operates: duties to follow rules and permitted uses are during-work, instructor set-up is before-course, institution-wide facts are general); (2) modality, informs vs must/should on sentences with no modal verb (resolved by the sentence's own wording); (3) unit_stance, where one coder gave rationale, penalty and procedure units a position (resolved to neutral) and narrow conditional permissions were split permit vs restrict (resolved to restrict); (4) type: P01 vs P06 for the Allen default ban (P01), P36 vs P06 for 'other uses are misconduct' (P36), P80 vs P51 for exceptions (P80), P50 vs P49 vs P79 for data and tool sentences (resolved by the stated reason in each sentence). Document stance differed once (UW-IT: delegates vs permit; resolved to permit because the page states support for responsible use and sets its own conditions). Coder A found 23 units coder B did not; 18 were kept (real statements such as scope, consequences, rationale and template lines) and 5 dropped (a pointer to the approved-tools list, three drafting-checklist questions folded into the checklist unit, and an implied 'may require AI' reading of a conditional sentence). Coder B found 3 units coder A missed or folded into another unit, all kept.
